<reason>Side A won the central methods clash. Side B argued stable-to-stable controls cheat by stripping the average, but A showed income, prior breakup, and foster drift harm any child and that law never purity-tests step, adoptive, widowed or donor straight families. B never justified why those confounds become intrinsic only for gay parents, nor why similar stable-stable outcomes should still lose protections. That left A's isolate-cause plus best-interests policy route live.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's stable-to-stable control plus double-standard turn in Rebuttal 1 and Rebuttal 2: breakup/disruption is not gay parenting, and straight non-biological families get full recognition, so denying it only to same-sex couples is selective punishment.</best_rebuttal>
